meta.note: Every quote is copied exactly from data/researchers.json with its source link. Sides are my own short summaries.

debates.q: Is superhuman AI only a few years away?
debates.why: If it is close, safety work and rules have very little time. If it is far, we can be more patient.

a.label: Yes, within years
a.blurb: These people expect AGI or superintelligence this decade, often by the late 2020s.

quotes.name: Leopold Aschenbrenner
quotes.text: AGI by 2027 is strikingly plausible.
quotes.source: Situational Awareness: The Decade Ahead

quotes.name: Sam Altman
quotes.text: We are past the event horizon; the takeoff has started.
quotes.source: The Gentle Singularity (blog)

quotes.name: Ilya Sutskever
quotes.text: Superintelligence is within reach.
quotes.source: Safe Superintelligence Inc. website

quotes.name: Daniel Kokotajlo
quotes.text: We predict that the impact of superhuman AI over the next decade will be enormous, exceeding that of the Industrial Revolution.
quotes.source: AI 2027 scenario (co-author)

b.label: Not so fast
b.blurb: These people think progress is real but slower, messier, or harder to predict than the headlines suggest.

quotes.name: Melanie Mitchell
quotes.text: The whole history of AI has been a history of failed predictions.
quotes.source: Munk Debate on AI, reported by The Hub

quotes.name: Arvind Narayanan
quotes.text: AI as normal technology is a worldview that stands in contrast to the worldview of AI as impending superintelligence.
quotes.source: AI as Normal Technology (with Sayash Kapoor)

quotes.name: Katja Grace
quotes.text: If science continues undisrupted, the chance of unaided machines outperforming humans in every possible task was estimated at 10% by 2027, and 50% by 2047.
quotes.source: Thousands of AI Authors on the Future of AI (lead author), arXiv

debates.q: Once AI can do AI research, will things explode?
debates.why: A fast takeoff leaves almost no time to fix mistakes. A slow one gives warning signs and second chances.

a.label: Fast and sharp
a.blurb: AI that builds better AI could compress decades of progress into months.

quotes.name: Leo Gao
quotes.text: The world is locked in a deadly race towards an intelligence explosion, where AI’s ability to create better AIs reaches a critical point, just like a runaway nuclear chain reaction. Going slower would give us much-needed time to make it go well, but no individual actor is willing to stop unilaterally.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

quotes.name: Will MacAskill
quotes.text: AI that can accelerate research could drive a century of technological progress over just a few years.
quotes.source: Preparing for the Intelligence Explosion (with Fin Moorhouse)

quotes.name: Jared Kaplan
quotes.text: is in some ways the ultimate risk, because it’s kind of like letting AI kind of go
quotes.source: Interview with The Guardian

b.label: Gradual and visible
b.blurb: Bottlenecks like compute, experiments and the real world slow things down, and we should see it coming.

quotes.name: Arvind Narayanan
quotes.text: AI as normal technology is a worldview that stands in contrast to the worldview of AI as impending superintelligence.
quotes.source: AI as Normal Technology (with Sayash Kapoor)

debates.q: Can we keep control of AI that is smarter than us?
debates.why: This is the heart of the safety problem. The answer decides whether we need better tools or a different path.

a.label: It may be impossible
a.blurb: Controlling something smarter than you, forever, has no precedent. We may get only one try.

quotes.name: Stuart Russell
quotes.text: The problem of control: how do we maintain power, forever, over entities that will eventually become more powerful than us?
quotes.source: US Senate hearing, Oversight of A.I. (statement page)

quotes.name: Geoffrey Hinton
quotes.role: Computer scientist, Nobel laureate in physics 2024
quotes.text: We have no idea whether we can stay in control.
quotes.source: Nobel Prize banquet speech

quotes.name: Roman Yampolskiy
quotes.text: you only get one chance.
quotes.source: Lex Fridman podcast, reported by Business Insider

quotes.name: Nate Soares
quotes.text: everyone dies on the first failed attempt.
quotes.source: Interview with Business Insider

b.label: It is hard but workable
b.blurb: With monitoring, testing and careful deployment, we can stay safe through the first powerful systems and learn as we go.

quotes.name: Ryan Greenblatt
quotes.text: We think no fundamental research breakthroughs are required for labs to implement safety measures that meet our standard for AI control for early transformatively useful AIs
quotes.source: The case for ensuring that powerful AIs are controlled (with Buck Shlegeris)

quotes.name: Buck Shlegeris
quotes.text: Labs should make sure that powerful models can't cause unacceptably bad outcomes even if the AIs try to.
quotes.source: The case for ensuring that powerful AIs are controlled (with Ryan Greenblatt)

quotes.name: Jeffrey Ladish
quotes.text: It’s great that we’re seeing warning signs before the systems become so powerful we can’t control them,
quotes.source: Interview with NBC News

debates.q: Should we slow down or pause frontier AI?
debates.why: A slowdown could buy time for safety, or could hand the lead to the least careful players.

a.label: Slow down
a.blurb: Racing makes everyone cut corners. Coordinated pacing, or a full stop, is the safer bet.

quotes.name: Eliezer Yudkowsky
quotes.text: Shut it all down.
quotes.source: TIME op-ed, Pausing AI Developments Isn't Enough

quotes.name: Victoria Krakovna
quotes.text: It is very important to build capacity for a coordinated slowdown of AI development. A runaway race to AGI is not safe: it creates incentives to cut corners on safety, and carries a substantial risk for model capabilities to outpace development of adequate alignment, control, and governance measures.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

quotes.name: Jakub Pachocki
quotes.text: I expect and hope for voluntary slowdowns to become commonplace until shared safety bars are established
quotes.source: Blog post, as quoted by CNBC

quotes.name: Ethan Perez
quotes.text: With the current rate of AI progress, safety teams at AI companies have to sprint to prevent new risks to society every few months. At some point, we’re going to hit problems we need more time to solve.
quotes.source: Pacing the Frontier, signatory comment

b.label: Keep building
b.blurb: The benefits are huge, the fears are overblown, and wide access is better than a pause.

quotes.name: Marc Andreessen
quotes.text: Fortunately, I am here to bring the good news: AI will not destroy the world, and in fact may save it.
quotes.source: Why AI Will Save the World (essay)

quotes.name: Andrew Ng
quotes.text: I have to admit that I struggle to see how AI could pose any meaningful risk for our extinction.
quotes.source: The Batch, letter from Andrew Ng (issue 200)

quotes.name: Sam Altman
quotes.text: We do need to solve the safety issues, technically and societally, but then it’s critically important to widely distribute access to superintelligence given the economic implications.
quotes.source: The Gentle Singularity (blog)

quotes.name: Dario Amodei
quotes.text: I think that most people are underestimating just how radical the upside of AI could be, just as I think most people are underestimating how bad the risks could be.
quotes.source: Machines of Loving Grace (essay)

debates.q: How likely is an AI catastrophe?
debates.why: People who agree on the facts still give very different odds. Seeing the spread helps you hold your own number loosely.

a.label: Worryingly likely
a.blurb: These people think catastrophe is a real, even large, possibility.

quotes.name: Eliezer Yudkowsky
quotes.text: Many researchers steeped in these issues, including myself, expect that the most likely result of building a superhumanly smart AI, under anything remotely like the current circumstances, is that literally everyone on Earth will die.
quotes.source: TIME op-ed, Pausing AI Developments Isn't Enough

quotes.name: Paul Christiano
quotes.text: Probability that humanity has somehow irreversibly messed up our future within 10 years of building powerful AI: 46%
quotes.source: My views on doom (LessWrong)

quotes.name: Toby Ord
quotes.text: And we’ve got unaligned artificial intelligence which is way out there at 1 in 10.
quotes.source: 80,000 Hours podcast

quotes.name: Evan Hubinger
quotes.text: I personally think it is >10% within the next decade,
quotes.source: Post on X, reported by CNBC

quotes.name: Demis Hassabis
quotes.text: What I would say is it’s definitely non-zero and it’s probably non-negligible.
quotes.source: Lex Fridman podcast, reported by Machine

b.label: Very unlikely
b.blurb: These people see AI as a tool that does not want anything, with ordinary risks we can manage.

quotes.name: Yann LeCun
quotes.text: There is no reason to believe that just because AI systems are intelligent they will want to dominate us.
quotes.source: Interview with WIRED

quotes.name: Marc Andreessen
quotes.text: In short, AI doesn’t want, it doesn’t have goals, it doesn’t want to kill you, because it’s not alive.
quotes.source: Why AI Will Save the World (essay)

quotes.name: Andrew Ng
quotes.text: AI has risks like bias, fairness, inaccurate outputs, job displacement, and concentration of power.
quotes.source: The Batch, letter from Andrew Ng (issue 200)

debates.q: Is AI a normal technology or something new?
debates.why: If it is normal, old tools like regulation and markets will work. If it is new, we may need new ideas.

a.label: Something new
a.blurb: Today's models are grown, not built, and even their makers cannot fully explain them.

quotes.name: Jack Clark
quotes.text: But make no mistake: what we are dealing with is a real and mysterious creature, not a simple and predictable machine.
quotes.source: Import AI 431, Technological Optimism and Appropriate Fear (talk at The Curve)

quotes.name: Sam Bowman
quotes.text: There are no reliable techniques for steering the behavior of LLMs.
quotes.source: Eight Things to Know about Large Language Models, arXiv

quotes.name: Beth Barnes
quotes.text: They are, in some sense, these vast alien intelligences,
quotes.source: Interview with TIME

quotes.name: Geoffrey Hinton
quotes.role: Computer scientist, Nobel laureate in physics 2024
quotes.text: There is also a longer term existential threat that will arise when we create digital beings that are more intelligent than ourselves.
quotes.source: Nobel Prize banquet speech

b.label: A normal technology
b.blurb: AI will spread slowly through society like electricity or the internet, and we should govern it that way.

quotes.name: Arvind Narayanan
quotes.text: AI as normal technology is a worldview that stands in contrast to the worldview of AI as impending superintelligence.
quotes.source: AI as Normal Technology (with Sayash Kapoor)

quotes.name: Yann LeCun
quotes.text: You don't want the digital diet of your citizens to be controlled by a small number of people.
quotes.source: Interview with WIRED

debates.q: Should the most powerful models be released as open weights?
debates.why: Open weights spread power and help research, but anyone can remove the safeguards.

a.label: Open is safer
a.blurb: Open models stop a few companies from controlling what billions of people see and think.

quotes.name: Yann LeCun
quotes.text: You don't want the digital diet of your citizens to be controlled by a small number of people.
quotes.source: Interview with WIRED

b.label: Be careful at the frontier
b.blurb: Once weights are public they cannot be recalled, so the most capable models need more caution.

refs.t: International AI Safety Report (2025), section on open weight models

pdoom.name: Geoffrey Hinton
pdoom.pdoom: 10% to 20% chance AI leads to human extinction within three decades

pdoom.name: Yoshua Bengio
pdoom.pdoom: About 20% that it turns out catastrophic

pdoom.name: Paul Christiano
pdoom.pdoom: 22% chance of AI takeover; 46% that humanity irreversibly messes up its future within 10 years of powerful AI

pdoom.name: Demis Hassabis
pdoom.pdoom: Definitely non-zero and probably non-negligible (no number given)

pdoom.name: Toby Ord
pdoom.pdoom: About 1 in 10 this century from unaligned AI
